messages:
mike-support: FYI customer on prod hitting 502s when calling hosted API over interface endpoint through TGW. They say it works from dev but prod times out or returns 502s intermittently. Attaching initial traces.

customer-rep: Session IDs 1234-5678, error snippet: "upstream read error: connection reset by peer". ~10% of requests fail, spike after noon deploy.

jordan-sre: can you paste dig + curl from their prod app host? suspect split-horizon DNS or PHZ caching with Route53 resolver.

mike-support: customer ran this from prod app host:
```
$ dig api.redwood.internal +short
10.45.12.34
$ curl -v https://api.redwood.internal/health
* Connected to 10.45.12.34 port 443
* TLS 1.2 connection established, but server sent RST
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
```
They also have TGW attachment in the central account and interface endpoint in prod subnets.

alice-ops: that IP 10.45.12.34 is the VPCE ENI IP? If client resolves to ENI it should go via interface endpoint — but if Route53 PHZ resolves to public IP then traffic would go out. Which resolver are they using?

customer-rep: their containers use the VPC resolver at 100.100.0.2 (forwarder to central PHZ). They recently enabled a shared PHZ in central account. Dev uses same config but in a different account.

jordan-sre: two hypotheses: 1) split-horizon caching TTL causing some hosts to have stale A -> public IP; 2) cross-account PHZ mis-association causing names to resolve to public ALB IP in prod but private in dev. Need tcpdump on prod app host to see destination IP and SNI.

mike-support: asked them to tcpdump. they returned:
```
14:12:01.123 IP 10.0.2.45.40982 > 10.45.12.34.443: Flags [S], seq 123
... TLS ClientHello SNI: api.redwood.internal
14:12:01.456 IP 10.0.2.45.40982 > 54.23.11.12.443: Flags [S], seq 789
```
So some flows hit 10.45.12.34 while others hit 54.23.11.12 (public).

alice-ops: aha — mixed resolution. Could be DNS caching at app layer or kube-dns caching at node level with old answer. Are they running CoreDNS with cache plugin? TTLs?

customer-rep: yes CoreDNS cache plugin with 300s TTL. They rolled a deploy at 13:00 and spike correlates with TTL expiry.

jordan-sre: workaround: flush CoreDNS cache and ensure resolver in VPC points to the interface endpoint PHZ target. Also check endpoint SG allows inbound from prod CIDR and that TGW route table doesn't prefer NAT for 10.* ranges (i.e., traffic to ENI should route locally).

mike-support: added steps to ticket and noticed TLS handshake resets when hitting ENI IP — could be ALB/NLB healthcheck flapping so proxy returns 502. Ask them to verify ENI targets healthy: `aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn <arn>` and `aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces --network-interface-ids eni-xxxx`.

alice-ops: quick commands I recommended:
```
# check kernel route to ENI from app host
$ ip route get 10.45.12.34
# flush CoreDNS cache
kubectl -n kube-system exec -it deploy/coredns -- coredns-cache clear || restart pod
```
Also recommended lowering cache TTL while they fix PHZ association.

customer-rep: flushed cache and traffic now consistently hits the ENI. 502s dropped to 0 in the last 30m. Looks like mixed DNS was root cause. Planning PHZ reassociation in central account and TTL change.

jordan-sre: follow-up actions: ask them to 1) update PHZ associations so prod queries resolve to interface endpoint IPs, 2) lower CoreDNS cache TTL temporarily, 3) add a VPCE endpoint policy to prevent accidental fallback to public IPs, and 4) enable TGW route propagation for the ENI subnets. We'll close after 24h stable.

devex-bot: Ticket #12345 updated: workaround applied. :white_check_mark:
